A bar chart of monthly revenue with a dashed target line, the latest bar highlighted, as drawn by a <Chart> with <Bar> and <Line> children.
Three buttons from one rocketstyle definition: primary in size md, danger as an outline, and a small one; every combination of state, size, variant and mode comes from the same definition.
A node graph: Webhook connects to Enrich and Archive, and Enrich connects to CRM. The edge from Webhook to Enrich is highlighted.
A small form: the Email field holds ada@example.com and shows the inline error "Already registered" from an async validator; the password field below is untouched.
One src/App.tsx compiles to ios/…/App.swift (SwiftUI) and android/…/App.kt (Jetpack Compose); the UI on the device is SwiftUI and Compose views, no JavaScript engine renders it. Experimental.
Code: const user = useQuery(() => ({ queryKey: ['user', props.userId], queryFn: () => fetchUser(props.userId) })). The key reads a prop, so a new userId refetches.

Three terminal lines: pyreon lint flags a destructured-props error (pyreon/no-props-destructure), pyreon check prints each fix for git-changed files, and pyreon doctor runs 15 gates and gives a 0–100 score.
Code: s.string().email().serverCheck('email-unique'). Cheap checks run in the browser; the server check is recorded as pending and runs on the server.
A route table: index.tsx is SSG, blog/[slug].tsx is ISR, account.tsx is SSR and (app)/dashboard.tsx is SPA. Every page picks its own rendering.
A signal trace runs into the Pyreon mark and on to three targets: web, iOS (SwiftUI, experimental) and Android (Compose, experimental).
4× less JavaScript than React 19 for the same app. Pyreon: 17.2 KB; React 19: 69.6 KB. same app, gzip -9, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
8.7× faster charts than ECharts 6. Pyreon: 4.36 ms; ECharts 6: 37.95 ms. one run, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.

6/6 operations won against React Flow 12. pan + zoom ×60: 210×; drag a node ×60: 7.25×; select node: 5.39×; unmount: 3.87×; add 50 nodes: 1.19×; mount 500: 1.17×. one run, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.

4/4 form operations won against six libraries. reset form: 9×; mount 12 fields: 3.05×; keystroke, blur: 2.42×; keystroke, validate: 1.8×. one run, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
12× faster t() than i18next. t(): 12×; interpolation: 5.1×; plural: 3.6×; number: 3.1×; date: 2.7×. one run, bun, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
4.7× faster renderToString than Solid. card: 4.68×; layout: 1.74×; list-1000: 1.72×; list-50: 1.64×. one run, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
2.6× faster than React 19 creating 10,000 rows. Pyreon: 72.6 ms; React 19: 192.0 ms. real Chromium, row board, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
6.5× faster server rendering than React 19. Pyreon: 109.9 µs; React 19: 714.4 µs. compiled SSR, one run, synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, record of 2026-11-05.
Side by side on each click: in the re-render model Counter, Label and Hint run again and are diffed; in Pyreon only the one text node in the button is written.

assets.alt: Schematic: Markdown posts flow into a typed collection and out to pages; each route carries its own render mode chip, SSG, ISR or SSR, and the collection also feeds an RSS feed.
Schematic: one .tsx file feeds three targets: a browser window labelled web, and two phones labelled SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose. Native targets are marked experimental.
Schematic: React components running on @pyreon/react-compat; two have already been converted to Pyreon components that run once, one is converting, and an MCP server gives the assistant the real API.
Schematic: a form, a table and a bar chart in one dashboard, all reading from one query; one table cell and one bar light up as the data changes.

assets.alt: The five migration steps as a loop: install the compat layer, change two config files, keep shipping, convert one component at a time, switch the compiler on. Six components of an app flip one by one from React-style (the body re-runs) to Pyreon (runs once) while @pyreon/react-compat sits underneath; at the last step the compat layer is switched off and jsxImportSource becomes @pyreon/core.

motion.reduced: end state: every component converted, compat off, ember underline under step 5

The Pyreon blog: the stories behind the numbers.
Pyreon: write it once in TypeScript, ship it fine-grained to the web, iOS and Android (experimental).
Pyreon: Your component runs once. Ever. A quarter of React's JavaScript. 2.6× faster at 10,000 rows.
Pyreon live stats.
40 products. One reactive core. The glyphs of all 40 Pyreon products.
Accessibility (@pyreon/a11y): One line, and screen readers hear “Saved”.
Forms: Type in one field. The other eleven never notice. 210 µs to mount a 12-field form. React Hook Form: 640 µs. TanStack Form: 680 µs.
Reactivity: Delete useMemo, useCallback and every dependency array. 2.1× faster effect propagation than Preact Signals (1,407 vs 2,874 ns, 100 effects)
Pyreon showcase: projects built with Pyreon.

Schematic: clicking Save calls announce('Settings saved'). The message passes through a polite live region that sighted users never see, and the screen reader speaks “Settings saved”. Later, navigating to /billing is announced as “Billing” by the router integration.

motion.reduced: static end state with the ember ring on the part that changed

assets.alt: A twelve-field form. Letters are typed into the email field one keystroke at a time; each keystroke pulses only the email input and its message, which reads "invalid" until the address is complete and then shows a check mark. The other eleven fields stay still and a counter reads 0 updates for them.

motion.reduced: static end state with the ember ring on the part that changed

assets.alt: Schematic signal graph: count.set(2) travels from the count signal to the computed double and on to the two places that read it, a Badge text node and a document.title effect. A separate theme signal and the class it feeds stay grey: they do not depend on count, so they never run.

motion.reduced: static end state with the ember ring on the part that changed

assets.alt: Example team chat: a channel list on a dark sidebar, a message thread with avatars and timestamps, and a connected status badge.
Example admin dashboard: four KPI cards, an area chart of revenue over 14 days and a bar chart of revenue by category, built with Pyreon query, charts and coolgrid.
Example invoice builder: a form for invoice details and parties on the left and a live invoice preview on the right, with export to HTML, Markdown, PDF and DOCX.
Example kanban board with To do, In progress and Done columns of cards with tags and assignees, undo and redo, and an admin/viewer role switch.
Example todo app with projects, priority and tag chips, an active/done filter that lives in the URL, and keyboard shortcuts listed in the sidebar.

The same small todo app, Today, built from one source file (examples/native-showcase/src/TodayApp.tsx) and running at once in Chromium (web, server-rendered and hydrated), an iOS Simulator (generated SwiftUI) and an Android emulator (generated Jetpack Compose), each screen shown from its status bar down to just below the list: three todos, typing "Pick up oat milk" and adding it, checking it off, removing it. Real screen captures with real input; waits shortened, typing sped up on the phones.
